title: Scope 2, Stage 4: extract server persistence by domain

requirements.expectation: The full scope of direct-Supabase-in-business-logic across the 5 named domains (jobs, payments, pairing, shop, identity) is inventoried before any slice starts, so slices are sized and sequenced deliberately rather than discovered mid-implementation.
requirements.verification: Parallel research across all 5 domains, cross-checked against each domain's actual files.
evidence: 56 non-test files across the 5 domains, ~32 touching Supabase directly. jobs and payments already have real adapter/boundary layers (job-store barrel; confirmation-store/durable-processing/payout-ledger/escrow-store) with a handful of route handlers bypassing them. pairing is a single 1459-line file with zero boundary and writes service_requests independently of jobs' job-store (two uncoordinated paths on one table). shop is 21 files, ~93% mixed, almost no boundary, and several admin routes have business logic with no domain-folder home at all. identity is only 3 files but ~15 caller routes duplicate direct profile-table queries instead of centralizing. Full detail in the paired .md guide's scope-research table.
Also flagged (out of Stage 4's named scope, same underlying problem): merit/merit-engine.ts and 7 other domain folders (callout, express, modules, push, reviews, security) under src/lib/server/.

requirements.expectation: The 3 payments route handlers that bypass existing payments adapters (init, refund, check-bank-unique) and payout-settlement.ts's loadProBank no longer call Supabase directly; behavior is unchanged.
requirements.verification: Diff review of each call site; grep for remaining direct .from(...) calls in these 4 files; unit tests for the new adapter and each route's existing behavior.
evidence: New src/lib/server/payments/bank-lookup.ts centralizes loadMotoristBankCode, loadProBankCode, loadMotoristBankDetails, loadProBankDetails, loadIdentityCheck, isBankAccountTaken. All 4 call sites (init/route.ts, refund/route.ts, check-bank-unique/route.ts, payout-settlement.ts) now import from it instead of calling createServiceSupabase() themselves. No behavior change: same queries, same tables, same null-on-error fallback (verified by diff, not just by running the new tests).

New tests: src/lib/server/payments/__tests__/bank-lookup.test.ts (11 tests covering each adapter function including the self-exclusion and payout_methods-last4 match cases), src/app/api/payments/init/__tests__/route.test.ts (4, including the self-payment-block path), src/app/api/payments/refund/__tests__/route.test.ts (4, including the gateway-refund-attempted path), src/app/api/payments/check-bank-unique/__tests__/route.test.ts (5, including the token-resolved-exclude-self path). None of these 3 routes had any test coverage before this slice.
Full suite (1,285 tests, 117 files), typecheck and lint all pass locally with 0 new warnings beyond one pre-existing unrelated warning (refund/route.ts's gatewayRaw, present before this slice).

requirements.expectation: There is one bank-account-uniqueness check, not two disagreeing implementations.
requirements.verification: Compare src/app/api/profile/update/route.ts's isBankAccountTakenByOtherUser against the new isBankAccountTaken in bank-lookup.ts.
evidence: Found during slice 1 research: src/app/api/profile/update/route.ts has its own isBankAccountTakenByOtherUser (lines 19-78) that duplicates check-bank-unique's old matcher but never checks payout_methods -- so the same bank account could be flagged 'taken' by one endpoint and not the other. Pre-existing, not introduced by slice 1. Deliberately not fixed in slice 1 (profile/update is outside 'payments route handlers' scope); tracked here so it isn't lost.

requirements.expectation: Payments-domain code does not directly mutate jobs-domain tables (service_requests) with job-state transitions; that belongs behind the jobs interface.
requirements.verification: Audit payout-settlement.ts and any other payments file for direct service_requests writes.
evidence: payout-settlement.ts's finalizeJobReleasedAfterPayout (line ~1320, unchanged by slice 1) reads and updates service_requests directly with job_version-guarded optimistic concurrency -- a jobs-domain state transition performed from the payments domain. Needs a job-store function (e.g. markJobReleasedAfterPayout) added to src/lib/server/jobs/job-store before payout-settlement.ts can stop touching the table directly. Deferred to a later slice since it's a cross-domain design decision, not a mechanical port.

requirements.expectation: The 3 jobs route handlers that bypass job-store (surface, dispatch-scheduled, expire-stale's zombie-reset) no longer call Supabase directly; behavior and the job_version/flow_status optimistic-concurrency guards are unchanged.
requirements.verification: Diff review of each call site confirming the exact same WHERE-clause guards and update payloads are preserved, not simplified; unit tests for the new job-store functions and each route's 403/404/409/500 paths; full suite green.
evidence: Confirmed against supabase/migrations/20261007_079_job_version_cas.sql that job_version is bumped by a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on every write to a service_requests row, unconditionally -- so a bare job_version guard is exactly as strong as the original compound guards (job_version + pairing_stage + pairing_deadline IS NULL for surface; job_version + flow_status for dispatch-scheduled). Decided to keep the original guards verbatim anyway rather than rely on this equivalence, matching the file's own existing convention (src/lib/server/jobs/job-store/dispatch.ts already has ~8 functions doing this exact raw-guarded-update shape, e.g. assignNextPro).

New src/lib/server/jobs/job-store/dispatch.ts functions armSurfacePairingDeadline and dispatchScheduledSecondPro verbatim-relocate the two routes' raw updates (same field lists, same WHERE clauses), returning a discriminated { ok, conflict, message } result instead of persist()'s thrown JobWriteConflictError, to preserve each route's existing inline 409/500 branching exactly. New src/lib/server/jobs/job-store/expiry.ts function resetZombieFlowStatuses verbatim-relocates the bulk zombie-reset update. All three exported from job-store/index.ts's barrel.

Deliberately did NOT route these through the generic persist()/jobToDbPatch helper: verifying jobToDbPatch covers every field these updates touch (flow_status, legacy status, pairing_stage, pairing_deadline, queue_position, remaining_candidates, reservation_status, assignment_status, pairing_radius_km, pickup_address/lat/lng, motorist_location_at) would be extra verification surface for no benefit, and a silent gap there would be a real regression (a dropped column on write).
surface/route.ts and dispatch-scheduled/route.ts now call getJob()/the new functions instead of raw Supabase; expire-stale/route.ts calls the job-store export instead of its own local helper.

Found and fixed an existing test (src/app/api/__tests__/second-pro-routes.test.ts) that mocked @/lib/server/jobs/job-store without the two new exports, which made 2 of its dispatch-scheduled tests fail after the rewire (the route now calls dispatchScheduledSecondPro, which the mock didn't provide, so it was undefined and threw). Updated the mock and rewrote the 3 affected tests to mock dispatchScheduledSecondPro's result directly instead of asserting on a raw Supabase update payload that no longer exists at the route level -- that payload-shape assertion now lives in the new job-store unit test instead.

New tests: src/lib/server/jobs/job-store/__tests__/dispatch.test.ts (8), src/lib/server/jobs/job-store/__tests__/expiry.test.ts (4), src/app/api/jobs/[id]/surface/__tests__/route.test.ts (7, this route had zero coverage before). Full suite (1,304 tests, 120 files), typecheck and lint pass with no new warnings (one pre-existing unrelated warning in expire-stale/route.ts, a dead `zombies` variable, confirmed unchanged by this diff).

requirements.expectation: A deliberate decision on whether/how to formalize an interface for the pairing domain, made after understanding why pairing-engine.ts is shaped the way it is -- not a mechanical application of the slice-1/2 pattern.
requirements.verification: Read docs/SSPE_REFACTOR_PLAN.md (the module's original design spec) and docs/ANTI_REGRESSION.md (mandatory before touching job-flow code) before proposing any change.
evidence: docs/SSPE_REFACTOR_PLAN.md section 6 shows pairing-engine.ts was deliberately designed as its own standalone module: 'idempotent, DB-first, advisory-locked per request', with each function doing an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE pairing_stage = expected in a single round-trip. This is not accidental tech debt -- splitting the read-check from the write across a 'business logic' file and an 'adapter' file would reopen the exact TOCTOU race the atomic single-statement UPDATE was built to close.

pairing-engine.ts already satisfies the spirit of Stage 4 for its own domain better than shop or identity do: every pairing/dispatch state mutation is concentrated in one file behind named, documented, idempotent exported functions (advancePairing, openRequest, confirmRequest, declineRequest, deferRequest, timeoutRequest, sweepPairing, sweepScheduledDispatches) -- it's just that each function still calls createServiceSupabase() inline rather than importing from a separate adapter file, which is a much smaller gap than shop's (zero concentration) or identity's (logic duplicated across ~15 routes).

Decision (stakeholder, 2026-10-10): skip a pairing refactor for Stage 4. Spend the risk budget on shop next, which has no atomicity pattern to accidentally break. The 'two uncoordinated paths write service_requests' finding from the original scope research (pairing-engine vs job-store/dispatch.ts's assignNextPro/rerouteDeclinedJob) was NOT independently verified before this decision -- whether those two code paths ever operate on the same job concurrently, or are mutually exclusive by job state (SSPE vs legacy dispatch), remains an open question, tracked below as remaining work rather than blocking this decision.

requirements.expectation: The 4 shop-admin route handlers that had real business logic + direct Supabase calls with no corresponding file in src/lib/server/shop/ (analytics, deliveries, couriers, product-requests) now delegate to domain functions; behavior is unchanged.
requirements.verification: Diff review of each route confirming identical queries/tables/payloads; unit tests for each new domain function and route; full suite green.
evidence: Ruled out a different first candidate: checkout/route.ts and delivery/estimate/route.ts both inline a user_addresses lookup, but user_addresses is also used by /api/addresses/route.ts and identity-sync.ts -- it's a cross-cutting concern shop doesn't own, not a shop-domain gap. Fixing it would invent an implicit 6th domain, out of scope for a shop slice.

New src/lib/server/shop/admin-analytics.ts (getShopDemandAnalytics), admin-couriers.ts (listCourierProviders, upsertCourierProvider, patchCourierProvider), admin-deliveries.ts (upsertDeliveryStatus), product-requests.ts (recordProductRequest, ProductRequestsNotMigratedError). Each verbatim-relocates its route's existing queries/payloads -- no behavior change.

Design grounded in existing src/lib/server/shop/ conventions, not invented: shop_audit_logs and shop_order_events inserts moved into the domain functions because admin-catalog.ts/orders.ts/payments.ts already do this at every write; logAdminAction (cross-cutting admin-identity audit, needs the route's requireAdmin() result) and requireAdmin()/isSupabaseAdminConfigured() stayed in the routes, matching every prior slice's routes-own-auth boundary.

New tests: src/lib/server/shop/__tests__/{admin-analytics,admin-couriers,admin-deliveries,product-requests}.test.ts (3+7+7+3=20) and src/app/api/{admin/shop/analytics,admin/shop/couriers,admin/shop/deliveries,shop/product-requests}/__tests__/route.test.ts (3+8+4+4=19). None of these 4 routes had any test coverage before this slice. Full suite (1,343 tests, 128 files), typecheck and lint pass with no new warnings beyond the pre-existing baseline (confirmed via git diff that the one new-looking warning, analytics route's unused _req param, was already unused before this slice).

requirements.expectation: Business services in the agreed scope use defined interfaces rather than Supabase SDK types or clients directly. (Same requirement id as the parent Stage 1-3 guide; Stage 4 is where it actually gets addressed, domain by domain.)
requirements.verification: Manual import audit of src/lib/server/{jobs,payments,pairing,shop,identity}, slice by slice.
evidence: Slice 1 (payments route handlers): done, see slice-1-payments-routes-no-direct-supabase above.
Slice 2 (jobs route handlers): done, see slice-2-jobs-routes-no-direct-supabase above.
Pairing: deliberately skipped, see pairing-interface-decision above.

Slice 3 (shop admin routes with no domain-folder home): done, see slice-3-shop-admin-routes-have-a-home above. Shop has 17 more direct-Supabase files remaining (cart, orders, catalog, admin-catalog, delivery, garage, import-engine, job-recommendations, search, all-parts, payments, import-job-detail, plus the checkout/delivery-estimate address-lookup duplication and the identity-adjacent user_addresses question) -- not started.
Remaining: rest of shop (17 files); identity (centralizing ~15 duplicated caller routes); the deferred jobs-payments-boundary-respected fix (finalizeJobReleasedAfterPayout).

implementationNotes: Stage 4 scoped via parallel research on 2026-10-10 (see domain-scope-researched evidence). Slice 1 (payments route handlers, commit 04bab32): new src/lib/server/payments/bank-lookup.ts adapter, 4 call sites rewired, 24 new tests. Slice 2 (jobs route handlers, commit 386a3e7): 3 new job-store functions, 3 routes rewired, 15 new tests, 1 existing test file fixed. Pairing deliberately skipped (see pairing-interface-decision). Slice 3 (shop admin routes with no domain-folder home), same day: 4 new src/lib/server/shop/ files (admin-analytics, admin-couriers, admin-deliveries, product-requests), 4 routes rewired, 39 new tests. Full suite (1,343 tests, 128 files), typecheck and lint pass after all 3 slices. Findings surfaced and tracked rather than silently fixed or ignored: a pre-existing bank-uniqueness-check inconsistency, a jobs/payments domain-boundary violation in finalizeJobReleasedAfterPayout, confirmation that job_version's DB trigger makes compound WHERE-clause guards provably redundant (kept anyway for verbatim-relocation discipline), and (slice 3) that the checkout/delivery-estimate user_addresses duplication isn't actually a shop-domain gap.
implementationState: Slices 1 (04bab32) and 2 (386a3e7) committed and pushed. Pairing deliberately skipped. Slice 3 (shop admin routes) complete locally, not yet committed -- awaiting review per the user's standing instruction to confirm before any commit.

Fix the jobs/payments boundary violation in payout-settlement.ts's finalizeJobReleasedAfterPayout (see jobs-payments-boundary-respected) -- requires a new job-store function.
